# Real-data evaluation

<!-- Generated by sim/sifted_sim/realeval.py with eval/sifted_realeval.cpp and eval/sifted_eval.cpp. Do not edit by hand. -->

How Sifted behaves on recorded aircraft data, as opposed to its own simulator ([evaluation.md](evaluation.md)), whose noise matches the filter's assumptions exactly and whose targets fly straight legs and constant-rate turns. Two complementary evaluations, on the same cleaned flights:

- **A, real measurements.** Real ADS-B positions through the real wire codec, decoder and engine. With no independent truth, it is scored predictively: runs of each aircraft's reports are withheld, and at each withheld report the tracker's estimate is compared with it, against two baselines (holding the last report; dead-reckoning it by its reported velocity).
- **B, real trajectories with simulated sensors.** The flight paths, interpolated, are the truth for the simulator's seeded radar and camera, scored by the same `sifted_eval` as the simulator scorecard; a constant-velocity control with identical sensors, noise and seeds separates the error caused by real motion from the error caused by noise.

All numbers on this page come from one command, run from the repository root on the cached data (download once with `python3 -m sifted_sim.realeval fetch`):

```bash
cmake --preset release && cmake --build --preset release
cd sim && python3 -m sifted_sim.realeval run
```

The page is a deterministic function of the cached data and the binaries: running the command twice gives a byte-identical file.

## Summary (held-out flights)

- **Prediction (A).** Median error of the tracker's estimate at a withheld report 8.8 m at 2–5 s horizons (dead reckoning 7.2 m), 36.1 m at 20–40 s (dead reckoning 25.8 m, holding the last report 5257.5 m) and 93.5 m at 40–80 s (dead reckoning 69.1 m).
- **Consistency (A).** Average NIS of real ADS-B updates 0.11 (2.00 expected for a consistent filter; 95% interval under independence [1.97, 2.03]) with the assumed 50 m ADS-B sigma: not consistent, innovations 0.23x the size the filter predicts.
- **Continuity (A).** 19 held-out engine runs (5 aircraft): 19 confirmed tracks, 0 fragmentations, 0 identity swaps (none possible: one aircraft per run), coverage 100.0% of reports after confirmation. At the live REST cadence (21.6 s polls, 5.4% of the reports): 2 fragmentations, coverage 99.6%.
- **Real motion, simulated sensors (B).** Position RMSE per window: median 13.8 m, p95 21.7 m, against 11.6 m / 13.4 m for the same sensors on a constant-velocity path; real motion accounts for 42% of the mean squared error. Truth quality limits this: leave-one-out interpolation error p95 27.4 m.

Unfavourable findings are listed under [Findings](#findings) and [Limitations](#limitations).

## Provenance

**Licence and terms.** Each archive's own README.txt states *Licence: CC BY 4.0* and asks for the citation below; the OpenSky Network's General Terms of Use & Data License Agreement (shipped with its other published datasets) also restrict use to non-profit research, education, or internal testing and evaluation, forbid redistributing the data, and require aircraft identifiers to be anonymised in publications and a copy of or link to any publication to be sent to OpenSky. To satisfy both, the archives are never committed (they are downloaded into the git-ignored `recordings/` directory and verified by SHA-256), no derived fixture is committed, and no address, callsign or registration appears in the results. Data: The OpenSky Network, https://opensky-network.org. Citation: M. Schäfer, M. Strohmeier, V. Lenders, I. Martinovic and M. Wilhelm, *Bringing up OpenSky: A large-scale ADS-B sensor network for research*, IPSN 2014.

## Method

**Selection.** Every flight that survives cleaning is used; none is chosen by hand. Flights are numbered by start time and every 3rd (F01, F04, ...) forms the tuning portion; the rest are held out. No tracker parameter is tuned at all; the two choices made from data, the interpolation method of evaluation B and the diagnostic sigma of evaluation A, are made on the tuning flights only. Headline numbers are held-out.

**Evaluation A.** Engine runs are flight chunks whose reports all lie within 300 km of the run's tangent-plane origin (its first report); chunks that overlap in time and fit within that radius share a run. The furthest report from an origin in these data is 300 km; at that range the flat-plane distortion of a straight constant-speed path is below 0.1% of its speed, far under the measurement noise. Engine configuration: the launcher's ADS-B settings (`--initial-velocity-sigma 250 --tentative-timeout 90 --coast-after 60 --drop-after 180 --max-position-sigma 10000`; `app/launcher.py` `ADSB_TRACKER_ARGS`), assumed sigma 50 m (`sifted_sim.adsb`). The estimator is the `EngineConfig` default, the IMM (ADR 0014); evaluation B's `sifted_eval` runs use the same default. Feeds:

- *all*: every cleaned report, at its millisecond position time (`lastposupdate`), nothing withheld. Continuity and NIS come from this feed.
- *withheld*: the same, minus the withheld reports: after 120 s, gaps of 2, 5, 10, 20, 40, 80 s in turn, each followed by 60 s of fed reports. Prediction errors come from this feed.
- *poll* / *poll withheld*: the live REST path. Every 21.6 s (the signed-in quota floor for a 1-credit box) each aircraft's latest report becomes an OpenSky state vector with whole-second `time_position` and goes through the real adapter (`sifted_sim.adsb.Adapter`), which drops repeats and stale or out-of-order positions.
- *all, default config*: the *all* frames with `EngineConfig` defaults (lifecycle sized for 1 Hz sensors), to show why the ADS-B settings exist.
- *sigma 6.8 m* (diagnostic): *all* and *withheld* with the assumed sigma replaced by one estimated on the tuning flights: the median leave-one-out error at spacing up to 2.5 s divided by 1.442 (the median of the Rayleigh distance of a report from the mean of its two neighbours, per unit sigma). Motion the interpolant misses and timing jitter inflate it, so it is an upper estimate. Nothing in the tracker or adapter defaults changes.

Horizon = withheld report time minus the aircraft's last fed report. The tracker's estimate is the operator picture at that time (`tracks_if_silent_until`): the track the aircraft's last fed report went to, if confirmed or coasting; otherwise it counts as *no track*. The aircraft label is used only to pick that track and to group results. Quantiles are nearest-rank. Definitions: `eval/sifted/eval/realdata.hpp`.

**Evaluation B.** Each flight is cut into consecutive 300 s windows; a window is used if reports cover it with no gap over 10 s (skipped: 33 window_knot_gap). The path is interpolated by **linear** (chosen on the tuning flights, below). A radar (the simulator's: 10 m, 0.2 deg, 1 Hz, Pd 0.9, 0.5 clutter/scan) with 20 km coverage sits 5 km left of the track at the window midpoint, and a camera (0.1 deg, 2 Hz) as far to the right; seeds 1, 2, 3. The control replaces the path by the straight line from its start to its end position over the same time. Scored by `sifted_eval --levels clean --match-distance 300` (direct engine feed, default `EngineConfig`): the simulator scorecard's 100 m match distance is sized for an 8 km radar, and the same rule (about four times the raw radar error at the coverage edge, 71 m here) gives 300 m. Windows whose reported heading ranges over more than 15 deg count as manoeuvring.

## Truth quality: interpolation (leave-one-out)

Each interior report is removed and predicted from its two neighbours; the error mixes interpolation error over twice the real spacing with the report's own noise, so it bounds the truth error of evaluation B from above. Median / p95 / max in metres, by neighbour spacing.

| held-out | linear | 21017 | 6.1 / 27.4 / 238.5 | 5.8 / 26.0 / 182.5 | 8.6 / 32.7 / 113.5 | 8.8 / 44.0 / 238.5 | 11.5 / 92.9 / 187.0 | 18.0 / 76.3 / 113.7 |

Chosen on the tuning flights (lower p95): **linear**. The two methods are nearly equal at the ~2 s spacing that dominates: at that spacing the error is mostly the reports' own scatter, not the interpolant.

### What the live REST path delivers

| portion | reports available | delivered by polling | stale |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| heldout | 21037 | 1137 (5.4%) | 28 |
| tuning | 17518 | 977 (5.6%) | 12 |

At a 21.6 s poll the tracker sees one report per aircraft per poll at most; the adapter's `repeat` drops are polls at which the aircraft had no newer position, `stale` ones are positions older than its 15 s limit. Its `older_than_sent` rule (and the engine's out-of-order rule) can only bite when aircraft with interleaved times share a response: each archive here holds one aircraft, so it did not.

## Findings

- **ADS-B noise assumption.** NIS 0.11 against 2.00: not consistent, innovations 0.23x the size the filter predicts, so the filter believes its innovations are larger than they are. The innovation covers the measurement noise and the filter's prediction error; the leave-one-out scatter of the reports themselves (held-out median 6.1 m at ~2 s spacing) is far below the assumed 50 m 1-sigma. The assumed value is left as it is (results here are not used to change defaults); see the diagnostic below for what a measured value does.
- **Prediction against dead reckoning.** The tracker's median error is above dead reckoning from the last report at horizons 0–2 s (8.4 m vs 7.0 m), 2–5 s (8.8 m vs 7.2 m), 5–10 s (11.7 m vs 9.1 m), 10–20 s (18.1 m vs 13.1 m), 20–40 s (36.1 m vs 25.8 m), 40–80 s (93.5 m vs 69.1 m), 80–160 s (377.4 m vs 168.9 m). Dead reckoning uses the aircraft's own velocity report, which the tracker never receives (GeoPosition carries position only): the tracker infers velocity from past positions, and none of its motion models anticipates a turn.
- **With the estimated sigma (6.8 m, diagnostic).** NIS 1.12, not consistent, innovations 0.75x the size the filter predicts; median tracker error 7.9 m at 2–5 s, 47.6 m at 20–40 s and 119.1 m at 40–80 s (assumed 50 m: 8.8, 36.1, 93.5 m); 18 fragmentations (assumed: 0). A measured noise level alone does not fix the tracker: it predicts worse and breaks more tracks, consistent with an estimator that then follows report noise more closely and, with a tighter gate, loses aircraft in turns. The 50 m value, though inconsistent, acts as smoothing the motion model needs; the mismatch is in the motion model as much as in the measurement noise.
- **Default lifecycle on real ADS-B.** With `EngineConfig` defaults the same input gives 146 tracks started, 61 confirmed and 42 fragmentations (ADS-B settings: 20, 19, 0); coverage 99.1% vs 100.0%.
- **Manoeuvres.** With simulated sensors, the median RMSE of manoeuvring windows is 15.1 m (p95 20.3 m) against 13.6 m for straight ones; the constant-velocity controls of the same windows give 11.4 m and 11.7 m.
- **Real motion breaks simulated-radar tracks.** On real paths 0 ID switches and 1 false tracks over 174 held-out runs, against 0 and 0 on the constant-velocity controls with the same sensors and seeds.
- **Large spread between flights.** The tuning windows give an RMS of 22.2 m against 15.2 m held out (controls 12.0 and 11.6 m): with 13 flights contributing windows, which flights land in a portion moves the result by more than the sensor noise does.

## Limitations

- **Sample.** 16 flights of 5 aircraft. The only real state vectors OpenSky still publishes openly are short incident extracts (diversions, emergencies, unusual flights), so the sample is small and biased towards unusual manoeuvres; it is not a traffic survey.
- **One aircraft per run.** Each extract holds a single aircraft, so no run has two aircraft in the same airspace: global nearest neighbour reduces to sequential gating of one track, and identity swaps, mixed tracks and dense terminal-area traffic cannot occur here. The metrics are implemented and tested on synthetic multi-aircraft input (`sim/tests/test_realeval.py`); measuring them on real traffic needs a multi-aircraft recording.
- **Sequential association.** Aircraft report at their own times, so a real ADS-B batch is almost always a group of one measurement: global nearest neighbour then behaves like sequential nearest-neighbour assignment, even with many aircraft.
- **2-D only.** The tracker discards altitude; vertical motion (climbs, descents, altitude separation of crossing aircraft) is not evaluated. Positions are compared horizontally in a tangent plane.
- **No independent truth.** Evaluation A scores against other ADS-B reports (which carry their own noise and OpenSky's receive-time stamping), and evaluation B's truth is interpolated ADS-B; both measure consistency with the aircraft's own reports, not absolute accuracy.
- **Isolated outliers pass cleaning.** The jump rule only rejects positions implying more than 400 m/s after 200 m of slack, so a single report a few hundred metres off survives; the leave-one-out maxima show them. They enter evaluation B's truth and evaluation A's withheld targets as they are (the rule was fixed before the results and is not tightened after seeing them).
- **Simulated sensors in B.** Radar and camera noise there still match the filter's assumptions exactly; only the motion is real.
- **OpenSky timing.** `time_position` in the live API has one-second resolution and positions can repeat; the poll emulation reproduces this, the *all* feed uses the archive's millisecond `lastposupdate`.

## Reproduction

```bash
cmake --preset release && cmake --build --preset release
cd sim && python3 -m sifted_sim.realeval fetch   # once; verifies every SHA-256
python3 -m sifted_sim.realeval run
```

Tests (offline, synthetic fixtures): `sim/tests/test_realeval.py` (parser, cleaning, interpolation, withholding, identity, end-to-end determinism when the binaries are built), `sim/tests/test_statevectors_fuzz.py` (property tests of the reader) and `Eval.*` in `tests/eval_test.cpp` (the scorecard is unchanged by the new scoring parameters).
